synthesis.body: `str.replace` on indented source matches ACROSS indent levels, because an 8-space pattern is a substring of the same text at 12 spaces. Rewriting call sites with `str.replace('        return x()', '        return self._x()')` also rewrites the helper's own body into a self-call — infinite recursion, and it happened once per client in a two-client change. The same class ate a newline in a YAML sweep and emitted `# v4.4.0with:`, which would have broken every workflow in the repository. Two mechanisms fix it. Anchor the rewrite to a whole line: iterate `splitlines()` and `re.match` with `^`, or require the match to be preceded by a newline. Then check the diff SHAPE afterwards — a pure call-site swap must be N insertions for N deletions, so any net line-count change means the pattern consumed something it should not have. Asserting the match count before replacing catches the other direction, where the anchor is not unique.

title: str.replace on indented Python matches across indent levels
